source: Wikimedia Pageviews API, human traffic only; brand identity from Wikidata
unit: reads per million reads of that edition (백만분율)
question: Does it change anything to split brands by kind instead of ranking them together?
answer: Yes. Indonesia sits 1st in one kind and 4th in another. Read as one lump, that disappears.

carsCompared.whyNotComparable: Only 1 of the 3 Korean marques has an article in all four editions. Hyundai has none in the Thai Wikipedia, and Genesis has one only in Indonesian. Putting a one-marque total against a three-marque total would not be a comparison between kinds; it would be a comparison between how many articles happen to exist. So no multiple is given here.
carsCompared.finding: The gap that stopped the comparison is itself the thing worth reporting: the Thai Wikipedia has an article on BMW, Mercedes-Benz and Porsche, and none on Hyundai.
carsCompared.notSales: This is how often an encyclopaedia article is opened, not how many cars are sold. We hold no sales figures here, so this page says nothing about who buys what, and a missing article is not a missing market. A marque with a century of motorsport carries model-by-model articles that a reader falls into; that alone can move reading without moving a single sale.

cannotAnswer: Wikidata records no ambassador or endorsement relation between people and brands. We checked and found none in use. So this cannot say who fronts which house. It measures how much a brand is read about, next to how much a person is read about, on one scale.
thinNote: A kind holding fewer than 3 brands is too thin to call a pattern. It is shown so the panel is complete, and marked so it is not read as one.
